bow_drill.backcountry.saw: Saw with ◀ and ▶ in turn (A and D)
bow_drill.backcountry.title: Bow Drill
cache.backcountry.ground: Within raiders' reach: a tall cache stands on 3 stripped logs stacked as poles
cache.backcountry.ladder: A ladder against the poles lets climbers in
cache.backcountry.scent: Scent attracts scavengers: keep it out of camp
cache.backcountry.spoiling: Spoils ×%s here (%s): a root cellar keeps it cooler
cache.backcountry.tall: Tall cache: out of reach of bears, wolverines and mice
condition.backcountry.blisters.began: Blisters, from walking in wet boots: you can't sprint. A dry day, a bandage or the Med Kit heals them.
condition.backcountry.blisters.cure: a dry day, a bandage or the Med Kit
condition.backcountry.burns.began: Burns: you stop healing. They pass in 2 days, sooner with a bandage, within a day with Pitch Salve; the Med Kit cures them.
condition.backcountry.burns.cure: a bandage halves it, Pitch Salve heals it in a day, the Med Kit cures it
condition.backcountry.exhausted.began: Exhausted after 2 days awake: your energy can't rise above half. Sleep: sneak and right-click the ground at night.
condition.backcountry.food_poisoning.beg: Food poisoning: you threw up your food and a litre of water. It passes in a day; the Med Kit cures it.
condition.backcountry.food_poisoning.cur: passes in a day, the Med Kit cures it
condition.backcountry.food_poisoning.fro: Food poisoning from %s: you threw up your food and a litre of water. It passes in a day; the Med Kit cures it.
condition.backcountry.frostbite.began: Frostbite: you are slower and can't sprint. 2 hours by a fire thaws it.
condition.backcountry.frostnip.began: Frostnip: your skin is starting to freeze. 2 hours by a fire thaws it.
condition.backcountry.gut_infection.bega: Gut infection, from unboiled water: you lose water twice as fast. It passes in 2 days; the Med Kit cures it.
condition.backcountry.gut_infection.cure: passes in 2 days, the Med Kit cures it
condition.backcountry.hypothermia.began: Hypothermia: your core is below 35 °C, so you are slow and can't sprint. Get warm and dry by a fire or under a roof.
condition.backcountry.hypothermia.cure: warm up by a fire or under a roof
condition.backcountry.infected_wound.beg: Infected wound: a fever burns more and you stop healing, and after 2 days it drains your health. A bandage halts it, Pitch Salve heals it within a day; the Med Kit cures it.
condition.backcountry.infected_wound.cur: a bandage halts it, Pitch Salve heals it in a day, the Med Kit cures it
condition.backcountry.numb_hands.began: Numb hands: the bow drill and handwork are clumsy. Wear mittens or warm your hands at a fire.
condition.backcountry.numb_hands.cure: mittens or a fire warm them back
condition.backcountry.parasites.began: Parasites, from raw meat: you absorb a quarter less of what you eat. Only the Med Kit cures them.
condition.backcountry.parasites.cure: only the Med Kit cures it
Rabbit starvation, from lean meat without fat: you absorb less and lose water. Eat fat: roasted animal fat, pemmican, salmon, marrow cracked from bones with a rock.
two days with enough fat end it
condition.backcountry.scurvy.began: Scurvy, from 8 days without vitamin C: you burn more and wounds heal at half speed. Berries, spruce tea, liver or raw fish cure it.
condition.backcountry.scurvy.cure: berries, spruce tea, liver or raw fish
condition.backcountry.severe_frostbite.b: Severe frostbite: you lose health until you are warm again. Get to a fire now.
condition.backcountry.severe_hypothermia: Severe hypothermia: your core is below 32 °C and you are dying. Get to a fire now.
condition.backcountry.shellfish_poisonin: Shellfish poisoning: your lips tingle and your legs go weak. There is no cure: lie still and let it pass.
passes in a few hours, no cure
cooking_pot.backcountry.empty: Empty: water and the foods of a recipe, an hour over a lit fire
cooking_pot.backcountry.mix_short: Nothing cooks from this mix: %s takes %s
fire.backcountry.coals_catch: Coals %s: add firewood and it catches
fire.backcountry.cold: Cold: light it with a bow drill or a ferro rod
fire.backcountry.packed: Packed too full: sparks may catch
hud.backcountry.hover.body: Your core temperature, and how the air feels through your clothes.
hud.backcountry.hover.energy.help: Work, cold and a heavy pack drain it; sleep and food restore it.
hud.backcountry.hover.energy.sprint: Below %s you are too tired to sprint.
hud.backcountry.hover.health.help: Comes back while energy and water are above a quarter and no infected wound or burn is open.
hud.backcountry.hover.spirits: Hot meals, new food, a fire, a warm room, sun, auroras, a big catch, a finished task, a new field note and company lift them; the same food, cold, wet, hunger, smoke and the dark lower them. High: work tires you less and you heal faster. Low: work is slower and sleep rests less.
hud.backcountry.spirits_bottom: Low spirits: you keep thinking of home
jade.backcountry.pot.boiled: Boiled water · safe to drink · %s L
jei.backcountry.birch_tap.note: Set on the side of a birch log in April and May: a quarter litre at a time, up to 2 L, free of gut infection.
jei.backcountry.camp_pot.boil: Hung over a lit fire: about 4 minutes at Steady, 2 at Hot. Boiled water carries no gut infection.
jei.backcountry.camp_pot.salt: Fill the Camp Pot at sea and keep it boiling for about 19 game hours: the water boils away and leaves salt.
jei.backcountry.camp_pot.syrup: 2 L of sap kept boiling for about 19 game hours boil down to syrup.
jei.backcountry.camp_pot.tea: Needles steep in the pot as it boils: vitamin C against scurvy.
jei.backcountry.cooking_pot: Stews on a lit fire for an hour with water poured in: %s servings, each using 0.25 L of water.
jei.backcountry.dressing: A %s kg animal: carry the carcass, set it down and dress it with a knife.
jei.backcountry.dressing.fat: Animal Fat %s to %s by the month: fattest in autumn, leanest in late winter.
jei.backcountry.dressing.heavy: A %s kg animal: too heavy to carry, dress it where it fell or haul it on a sled.
jei.backcountry.drying_rack: Hung on a Drying Rack it dries in %s dry days, twice as fast over a lit fire; rain and snow stop it. Dried food keeps for months and weighs half.
jei.backcountry.gathering.bark: Strip a birch log with an axe, standing or laid.
jei.backcountry.gathering.clams: Dig beach sand with a shovel: clams %s%% of the time
jei.backcountry.gathering.cricket: Grass and ferns cut from June to August: %s%% of the time.
jei.backcountry.gathering.driftwood: Driftwood washes up on beaches, already seasoned, most after a gale
jei.backcountry.gathering.flint: Gravel broken by hand or tool sometimes gives flint.
jei.backcountry.gathering.fungus: Use a bark mushroom on a burning fire: it smoulders %s hours and lights a cold one
jei.backcountry.gathering.goose_eggs: Goose nests by the lakes in May hold 2 to 4 eggs
jei.backcountry.gathering.iron: Iron-flecked gravel in birch-forest pits and stream beds, dug with a shovel: Raw Iron %s%% of the time.
jei.backcountry.gathering.mussels: Mussel beds grow on stony shores at the waterline: pick them by hand
jei.backcountry.gathering.needles: Break spruce leaves with a knife.
jei.backcountry.gathering.pitch: Sneak and use an axe on a spruce's side to blaze it; after %s days scrape the pitch with a knife
jei.backcountry.gathering.roots: Dig beside a spruce with a shovel: roots %s%% of the time
jei.backcountry.gathering.string: Natural cobwebs in the woods give string: a knife cuts them quickly.
jei.backcountry.gathering.worm: Dig grass or dirt with a shovel above freezing: %s%% of the time, %s%% within 12 hours after rain.
jei.backcountry.info.bandage: Halts an infected wound and halves the time burns take to pass.
jei.backcountry.info.bear_spray: Hold right-click to spray a cone 4 blocks long, 8 bursts a can: any charge ends and the animal flees for 30 seconds. Sprayed point-blank, it blinds you too.
jei.backcountry.info.binoculars: Worn at the neck or carried in the hotbar, C looks through them at 8 times; holding use does the same in hand. Watching an animal for 2 seconds notes it.
jei.backcountry.info.camp_pot: Holds 4 L. Fill it at a lake or stream and hang it on a lit campfire: it boils in about 4 minutes at Steady. Lifted off, it keeps how far it boiled. Sea water boils down to salt.
jei.backcountry.info.campfire: Light it with a Tinder Bundle, 2 sticks of kindling and a Bow Drill or Ferro Rod, then feed it seasoned firewood. Food laid on it cooks and a pot hangs on it. Stand in it a second and it burns you.
jei.backcountry.info.cooking_pot: Set on a campfire. Water and the foods of a recipe, an hour over a lit fire, make a stew; Animal Fat renders in pairs. Right-click it to see what it makes.
jei.backcountry.info.food_cache: The rations eat from caches within 64 blocks at 06:00 and 18:00. On 3 stripped logs stacked as poles, bears, wolverines and mice can't reach it; a root cellar keeps it cool.
jei.backcountry.info.headlamp: Worn on the head, it lights the dark and stays dark in daylight. A full charge lasts 8 hours of darkness; deep cold dims it.
jei.backcountry.info.med_kit: 4 uses: each cures at once every condition the kit can cure. It gives back no hearts.
jei.backcountry.info.moose_call: Blow it during the rut in September and October: a bull answers and comes from out of sight. Once every 2 minutes.
jei.backcountry.info.moose_head: With 2 L of water, an hour in the Cooking Pot over a lit fire makes 8 bowls of Moose Head Soup. It spoils like raw meat.
jei.backcountry.info.plant_fibre: Sneak and right-click to let a few strands drift with the wind: they show where your scent goes. Two make a Bandage.
jei.backcountry.info.satellite_messenger: Right-click: the weather, warmth, food, body, tasks, the year, your field notes and the Guide. A new alert beeps and lights its icon. SOS taps out.
jei.backcountry.info.sled: Set it down like a boat and pull it on a lead: it glides on snow, drags on bare ground and carries a whole moose.
jei.backcountry.info.smoker: Hang raw or cooked meat and fish over smouldering firewood: a batch smokes in 12 hours of rising smoke and then keeps for months.
jei.backcountry.info.snowshoes: Worn on the feet: deep snow costs far less to wade through and no longer freezes your feet.
jei.backcountry.info.water_bottle: Holds 1 L. Fill it at a lake or stream, or from a Camp Pot that has boiled; unboiled water can make you ill a day later.
jei.backcountry.lighting: Right-click the campfire with a Tinder Bundle and 2 sticks of kindling in it, then with the Bow Drill or Ferro Rod. Pitch Tinder catches in rain.
jei.backcountry.lighting.fungus: A smouldering bark mushroom lights a cold fire's tinder and kindling without a bow drill.
jei.backcountry.maps: A drawn Birch-Bark Map and a blank one in the crafting grid: both share the drawing from then on.
jei.backcountry.salting: Salt and raw meat or fish in the crafting grid: it keeps 8 times as long.
jei.backcountry.sharpening: A worn knife, axe or saw and the Sharpening Stone in the crafting grid: %s%% of its wear back. The stone lasts %s sharpenings.
jei.backcountry.smoker: Hung in the Smoker over smouldering firewood: %s hours of rising smoke cook and smoke it, keeping 64 times as long.
jei.backcountry.traps.deadfall: Set on the ground, baited with a cricket. Keeps mice off caches within 8 blocks.
jei.backcountry.traps.fish_wheel: In a stream two blocks deep: up to %s salmon a day in the run, %s whitefish or grayling otherwise
jei.backcountry.traps.gill_net: Set in still water: about two fish a day.
jei.backcountry.traps.large_snare: Set within 2 blocks of water, baited with a cricket.
jei.backcountry.traps.mouse_trap: Keeps mice off caches within 8 blocks.
jei.backcountry.traps.small_snare: Set on the ground, baited with a cricket; twice the odds on a hare run with fresh prints.
jei.backcountry.traps.tip_up: Set over a hole in lake ice: about two fish a day, twice as many baited with Game Guts.
jei.backcountry.woodpile.note: Laid on a woodpile it dries 12.5%% a day, half as fast below freezing and not at all while rain or snow falls on it.

message.backcountry.canvas_pack: You put on a Canvas Pack

message.backcountry.fell_off: The raft pitched and you fell off
message.backcountry.fish_wheel_stream: A fish wheel needs a stream two blocks deep
message.backcountry.fungus_lit: The fungus takes an ember and smoulders
message.backcountry.needles_in: Needles in: it steeps as the pot boils
message.backcountry.needles_need_water: Needles steep only in a pot of plain water
message.backcountry.needs_kindling: Needs a tinder bundle and %s sticks of kindling
message.backcountry.needs_knife: Needs a knife: the Belt Knife or a Knife
message.backcountry.nothing_to_treat: Nothing to treat: hearts come back on their own while energy and water are above a quarter
message.backcountry.pot_spoiled: Spoiled: it won't go in the pot
message.backcountry.rack_rained: Rain and snow stop the drying: roof the rack
message.backcountry.rack_refuses: Only raw meat or fish dries on the rack
message.backcountry.raided_bear: A bear broke into a cache and ate %s: a cache on 3 stripped logs is out of its reach
message.backcountry.raided_wolverine: A wolverine raided a cache: it ate %s and fouled what it left. A cache on 3 stripped logs is out of its reach
message.backcountry.salt_water: Sea water is salt: fill it at a lake or river
message.backcountry.sea_water_in_pot: Sea water is salt: boil it dry on a fire for salt
message.backcountry.sleep_on_ground: You can only sleep with your feet on the ground
message.backcountry.smothered: Snow fell from the spruce and smothered the fire
message.backcountry.survey.charcoal: Surveying needs a piece of charcoal
message.backcountry.survey.done: You sketch what you can see
message.backcountry.too_cold_to_sleep: Too cold to sleep here: by a fire, under a roof or in a Sleeping Bag
message.backcountry.too_heavy: Too heavy to carry: dress it here
messenger.backcountry.guide.caches.text: A cache holding 1,024 kcal of meat or fish smells: bears, wolves and wolverines come twice as often within 64 blocks. A bear eats from a ground cache and a wolverine eats and fouls a stack, unless you are within 16 blocks. Set the cache on 3 stripped logs stacked as poles and bears, wolverines and mice can't reach it; a ladder beside the poles lets them up. Food keeps longer in the cold: a root cellar dug into the ground stays cool in summer. Keep the cache within 64 blocks of where you are at 06:00 and 18:00 for the rations.
messenger.backcountry.guide.coast.text: Beaches collect driftwood, already seasoned, most after a gale. A shovel in beach sand turns up clams, and mussels grow on stony shores at the waterline. Shellfish poison 1 time in 32, 1 in 8 from June to August: slowness and hearts draining for 4 hours, and no cure. Cooking doesn't help. Geese nest by the lakes in May, 2 to 4 eggs a nest.
messenger.backcountry.guide.cold.text: Wind, rain and night air cool your core. Below 35 °C it is hypothermia and you can't sprint; below 32 °C you are dying. A fire, a roof and dry clothes warm you back. Bare skin freezes at -15 °C: wear a hat, and mittens, or an hour of bare hands goes numb and the bow drill and the knife fumble. Hide clothing keeps out a winter night; a Fur Parka, its hood over your head, keeps out the worst.
messenger.backcountry.guide.fat.text: Lean meat alone starves you: more than 300 g of protein a day with fat under a quarter of your kcal, two days running, brings rabbit starvation. You absorb less and lose water twice as fast until two fatty days end it; no Med Kit cures it. Bears are fattest in autumn, moose and caribou in the rut, hares never. Roast fat on a fire to eat it now, render it in the Cooking Pot to keep it for months, crack bones with a rock for marrow, and make pemmican or akutaq to carry it.
messenger.backcountry.guide.fire.text: A Bow Drill or a Ferro Rod lights a campfire from a Tinder Bundle and 2 sticks of kindling; Pitch Tinder catches even in rain. A bark mushroom held to a burning fire smoulders for 2 hours and lights a cold one without the drill. Feed firewood seasoned 50% or more: green wood won't catch, and drier wood burns hotter. When the queue burns out the fire settles to coals; firewood added while they glow catches. Snow sliding off spruce branches can smother a fire beneath them.
messenger.backcountry.guide.food.text: Raw meat gives parasites 3 times in 5: cook it on a lit campfire, heart, liver, tongue and kidney too. Food spoils faster in warmth and keeps frozen; smoked meat keeps for months. The Cooking Pot makes stews, renders fat and turns a moose head into soup.
messenger.backcountry.guide.health.text: Hearts come back on their own while energy and water are above a quarter, twice as fast asleep, unless a wound is infected or burnt. A Bandage of plant fibre halts an infection and soothes burns; Pitch Salve heals either within a day. The Med Kit cures most conditions at once but gives back no hearts.
messenger.backcountry.guide.hunting.text: Big game leaves prints in snow, mud, sand and dirt, and droppings on any ground. Sneak and look at sign to read whose it is and how old, and follow it the way it gets fresher. Moose and caribou smell you from downwind: check the wind with Plant Fibre and stalk into it. An arrow to the chest drops big game; any other hit wounds it, and it bleeds a trail. A bear takes 3 arrows to the chest, 2 from the heavy bow, and comes for whoever shot it; anything else only angers it.
messenger.backcountry.guide.ice.text: New ice is thin and thickens a step each freezing day until it holds anything. The thinnest gives way under anyone; the next under 16 kg of load or a sled; the next under a sled carrying 64 kg. Listen for cracking. Overflow slush on river ice soaks your feet. In April the ice rots from the edges: the breakup alert warns you off it. A sled glides on ice.
messenger.backcountry.guide.rations.text: At 06:00 and 18:00 you eat half the team's daily ration on your own: from Food Caches within 64 blocks, soonest to spoil first, or from what you carry when no cache is in reach. Chests never feed the rations, and raw food doesn't count. Set Lean, Normal or Feast at a cache; the Food page shows the next meal and the stores in days.
messenger.backcountry.guide.rock.text: Solid rock breaks slowly with stone tools; loose rocks on the ground make cobblestone, 4 to a block. Iron is dug, not mined: a shovel in iron-flecked gravel, in birch-forest gravel pits and the beds of streams and lakes, turns up Raw Iron 1 dig in 4. It smelts in a furnace, and an Iron Ingot alone in the crafting grid makes 9 nuggets.
messenger.backcountry.guide.rooms.text: A sealed room, walls, floor and roof with no gap, at most 16 blocks across and 8 high, holds its heat and warms toward its fire over about an hour; food inside keeps to the room's air. A campfire indoors needs an open block in the roof straight above it, or smoke fills the room: sleep does half its good and spirits sink. A Stone Fireplace burns at half the wood and vents up a Stone Chimney. A snow shelter holds about -2 °C on your own heat at -40, and a sealed room at least half in the ground keeps near 4 °C: a root cellar.
messenger.backcountry.guide.spirits.text: A warm fire, a warm room, sun and company hold your spirits up to the middle; a hot meal, a new food, a big catch, a finished task and the northern lights lift them higher, and above the middle they settle back over days. Cold, hunger, wet, illness, long dark, a smoky room and the same food again and again wear them down. High spirits make work cheaper and heal you faster. Low spirits slow your hands and make sleep do less. At the bottom the SOS button glows; nothing else happens, but you keep thinking of home.
messenger.backcountry.guide.water.text: Fill the Camp Pot at a lake or stream and hang it over a lit campfire: it boils in about 4 minutes, sooner on Hot. Sea water boils down to salt, not drinking water. Unboiled lake water makes you ill a day later 1 time in 4 a litre, stream water 1 in 16. Food holds water too: fruit most, cooked meat more than half its weight. Sneak and right-click to pour a vessel out.
messenger.backcountry.guide.wayfinding.t: A Birch-Bark Map is drawn only where you survey: climb high in daylight with no rain or snow falling, sneak and hold use with charcoal in your pack, and a quarter hour later it shows what you can see, farther from higher ground, with a cross where you stood. It has no arrow; find yourself by the land. Copies made from blank maps share the drawing. Blaze trees with an axe (sneak and use on a log's side) and pile rocks into cairns, up to 3 high, to mark a trail.
messenger.backcountry.guide.wildlife.tex: Wolves and coyotes keep their distance and hunt hares, caribou and beavers; hit one and its pack fights back. Grizzlies come at you in spring and autumn, and most charges stop short if you stand still: never run. Black bears flee unless they guard cubs or food. A moose cow with a calf in May and June, or a bull in the rut, may charge; most are bluffs, and a tree trunk between you stops it. The Bear Spray ends any charge. Porcupine quills punish a bare hand.
messenger.backcountry.help.cold: Get to a fire or under a roof, and dry off.
messenger.backcountry.help.energy: Sleep, food and rest bring it back.
messenger.backcountry.help.lean: More than %s g of protein with little fat: eat fat or rabbit starvation sets in.
messenger.backcountry.help.load: Over your capacity energy drains faster: leave something in a chest or cache.
messenger.backcountry.help.room: Close the walls and the door: a sealed room holds a fire's warmth.
messenger.backcountry.help.smoky: Smoke fills the room: open one block in the roof straight above the fire, or build a Stone Fireplace with a chimney.
messenger.backcountry.help.stores: Put food in a Food Cache: the rations eat from caches within %s blocks.
messenger.backcountry.help.thin: Eat more than you burn: at BMI %s you are extracted.
messenger.backcountry.help.water: Drink about 3 L a day; boiled water is safe.
messenger.backcountry.help.wet: A fire dries you; rain, snow and wading wet you.
messenger.backcountry.help.wind: A roof within 4 blocks overhead takes the wind off.
messenger.backcountry.notes.none: Nothing noted yet. Watch an animal through the binoculars, take one, land a fish or pick a plant, and it goes in your notes.
messenger.backcountry.notes.title: Field notes
messenger.backcountry.nutrients: Protein %s g · carbs %s g · fat %s g (%s of kcal)
messenger.backcountry.sos.arrival: A new survivor arrives at the drop-off.
messenger.backcountry.sos.boat: A boat picks you up, and your run ends here.
messenger.backcountry.sos.pack: Your pack stays where you stand.
messenger.backcountry.sos.question: Send SOS and tap out?
messenger.backcountry.year.berries.quiet: Last berries kept on the bush
messenger.backcountry.year.calves.full: Cows guard their calves: keep away
messenger.backcountry.year.mosquitoes.fu: Mosquitoes near water from dusk to dawn
messenger.backcountry.year.salmon_run.fu: Salmon run up the streams, and bears fish them
rack.backcountry.spoils_first: %s · %s%% dry · spoils before it dries: hang it in the cool or over a fire
ration.backcountry.dawn_full: Dawn ration: %s · %s kcal, too full for more
ration.backcountry.dawn_none: No food for the dawn ration: rations eat from a Food Cache within %s blocks or what you carry, never from chests.
ration.backcountry.dusk_full: Dusk ration: %s · %s kcal, too full for more
ration.backcountry.dusk_none: No food for the dusk ration: rations eat from a Food Cache within %s blocks or what you carry, never from chests.
ration.backcountry.how: Rations: at 06:00 and 18:00 you eat on your own. Set the ration at a Food Cache.
summary.backcountry.year_line: %s survivors on the island this year
summary.backcountry.year_line_one: %s survivor on the island this year
task.backcountry.axe.axe: Lash a Stone Axe, or carry the kit's Axe
task.backcountry.axe.axe.how: A Rock, a Stick and a Cordage in the crafting grid.
task.backcountry.axe.cordage.how: Break grass and ferns for Plant Fibre; 4 twist into a Cordage.
task.backcountry.axe.rock.how: Rocks lie loose on the ground; break one to pick it up.
task.backcountry.axe.stick.how: Twigs lie on the forest floor; each makes a Stick in the crafting grid.
task.backcountry.axe.why: A log takes an axe: bare hands get nothing from a tree.
task.backcountry.boil_water.drunk.how: Drink from the pot, or fill the Water Bottle from it.
task.backcountry.boil_water.filled.how: Right-click a lake, river or stream with it.
task.backcountry.boil_water.hung.how: Right-click the top of a lit campfire with the pot. It boils in about 4 minutes, rolling under thick steam once it is safe; sneak and look at it to see how long is left.
task.backcountry.boil_water.why: Unboiled water makes you ill a day after you drink it: lake water 1 time in 4, stream water 1 in 16. Do the steps in order.
task.backcountry.build_cabin.fire.how: A campfire needs an open block in the roof straight above it, or the room fills with smoke. A Stone Fireplace (cobblestone, a clay ball and a campfire) with a Stone Chimney burns at half the wood.
task.backcountry.build_cabin.room.how: Walls, floor and roof with no gap, at most 16 blocks across and 8 high. Doors and trapdoors count when shut; the Messenger's Warmth page says Cabin when it holds.
task.backcountry.build_cabin.slept.how: Sleep inside: sneak and right-click the floor at night.
task.backcountry.build_cabin.why: A sealed room with a fire holds its heat through the night.
task.backcountry.build_cache.cache: Set it down out of camp
task.backcountry.build_cache.cache.how: 7 planks and a Cordage in the crafting grid; set it down 16 blocks or more from a campfire.
task.backcountry.build_cache.food.how: Cooked, smoked and dried food count; raw food does not.
task.backcountry.build_cache.planks.how: Right-click a log with the axe to strip it; a stripped log and the axe make 4 planks.
task.backcountry.build_cache.why: The rations eat from caches within 64 blocks; meat in one draws bears, so it stands out of camp.
task.backcountry.build_canoe.canoe.how: 4 Birch Bark, Spruce Roots and Spruce Pitch in the crafting grid.
task.backcountry.build_canoe.pitch.how: Sneak and use an axe on a spruce's side to blaze it; after 2 days scrape the pitch with a knife.
task.backcountry.build_canoe.roots.how: Dig dirt beside a spruce with a shovel.
task.backcountry.build_canoe.why: Rivers and lakes are the island's roads.
Put a log in the furnace with wood below to burn.
task.backcountry.build_furnace.furnace: Build the furnace and set it down
task.backcountry.build_furnace.furnace.h: 8 cobblestone in a ring in the crafting grid.
task.backcountry.build_furnace.torch.how: Charcoal over a Stick. A torch burns 36 hours; charcoal tops it up.
task.backcountry.build_furnace.why: A furnace burns charcoal for torches and smelts iron.
task.backcountry.cook_meat.eaten.how: Right-click a lit campfire with raw meat, fish, heart or liver, take it off cooked and eat it. Fat roasts too.
task.backcountry.cook_meat.why: Raw meat carries parasites 3 times in 5.
task.backcountry.cook_stew.pot: Set a Cooking Pot on a campfire
task.backcountry.cook_stew.pot.how: 5 Iron Ingots in the crafting grid.
task.backcountry.cook_stew.served.how: Pour in 2 L of water, add the foods of a recipe and keep the fire lit for an hour; a bowl serves it.
task.backcountry.cook_stew.why: A Cooking Pot turns meat, roots and a moose head into stews that also give you water.
task.backcountry.cure_hide.cured.how: A Scraped Hide and Rendered Fat in the crafting grid.
task.backcountry.cure_hide.fat.how: 2 Animal Fat in the Cooking Pot over a lit fire.
task.backcountry.cure_hide.pot.how: 5 Iron Ingots in the crafting grid. It stands on a campfire for stews and rendering; the Camp Pot only boils water.
task.backcountry.cure_hide.scraped.how: A pelt or a rabbit hide and the knife in the crafting grid.
task.backcountry.cure_hide.why: Cured hides make clothing for the cold and the Hide Pack.
task.backcountry.draw_map.map.how: 4 Birch Bark and Cordage in the crafting grid.
task.backcountry.draw_map.surveyed.how: Climb high in daylight with no rain or snow falling, then sneak and hold use: a quarter hour and a piece of charcoal for each.
task.backcountry.draw_map.why: The island is big, and a map of what you've seen brings you home.
task.backcountry.dry_firewood: %s pieces of dry firewood on woodpiles
task.backcountry.dry_firewood.dried.how: Wood dries for days on a woodpile: lay it early and roof it.
task.backcountry.dry_firewood.why: Green wood will not catch in winter.
task.backcountry.dry_fish.dried.how: Hang up to 4 raw fish and wait 2 dry days; a fire up to 2 blocks below dries twice as fast, and rain stops it.
task.backcountry.dry_fish.rack.how: 6 sticks and 2 Cordage in the crafting grid.
task.backcountry.dry_fish.why: Dried fish weighs half and keeps for months.
task.backcountry.eat_berries.eaten.how: Salmonberries ripen in June, blueberries in July. Baneberries, white with a black eye, are poison.
task.backcountry.eat_berries.why: Berries carry vitamin C against scurvy.
task.backcountry.field_notes.noted.how: Watch an animal through the binoculars, take one, land a fish or pick a plant. The Messenger's Notes page keeps them.
task.backcountry.field_notes.why: Knowing what lives here tells you what to eat, what to hunt and what to keep away from.
task.backcountry.fill_bottle.drunk.how: Hold right-click with the Water Bottle; it arrived full of boiled water.
task.backcountry.fill_bottle.filled: Refill it from the boiled pot
task.backcountry.fill_bottle.filled.how: Right-click the Camp Pot with the bottle once the water has boiled. A bottle of boiled water drinks when aimed at a lake, so it never takes in lake water.
task.backcountry.fill_bottle.why: You need about 3 L of water a day, and the bottle holds 1 L.
task.backcountry.fish_wheel.catch.how: Up to 4 salmon a day in the run, a whitefish or grayling otherwise.
task.backcountry.fish_wheel.wheel: Set a Fish Wheel in a stream
task.backcountry.fish_wheel.wheel.how: 4 sticks, 4 Rope and a log in the crafting grid; set it in moving water two blocks deep.
task.backcountry.fish_wheel.why: The current turns it day and night: fish while you sleep.
task.backcountry.food_stores: %s days of food in the caches
task.backcountry.food_stores.stored.how: Smoked meat keeps for months; the Food page counts the days at the team's ration.
task.backcountry.food_stores.why: Winter brings little to hunt; stores carry the team through it.
task.backcountry.fur_parka.parka.how: 8 Cured Hides and the Wolverine Pelt in the crafting grid.
task.backcountry.fur_parka.pelt.how: Dress a wolverine. Frost brushes off its fur, so it makes the ruff.
task.backcountry.fur_parka.why: The warmest coat, and its hood keeps your head warm under a headlamp.
task.backcountry.hide_clothing.coat.how: Cured hides in the crafting grid; anyone in the team counts.
task.backcountry.hide_clothing.hat.how: Cured hides in the crafting grid; anyone in the team counts.
task.backcountry.hide_clothing.snowshoes: Rawhide strips and Sticks; without them deep snow halves your speed.
task.backcountry.hide_clothing.why: The clothes you arrived in will not keep out -30 °C.
task.backcountry.hide_pack.pack.how: Cured hides in the crafting grid.
task.backcountry.hide_pack.why: It opens a second row above the hotbar.
task.backcountry.hide_pack.worn.how: Put it in the back slot beside the armour. Empty the Canvas Pack first: a pack keeps its items when it comes off.
task.backcountry.ice_fishing.auger.how: 3 Iron Ingots and a Stick in the crafting grid.
task.backcountry.ice_fishing.catch.how: Check it the next day; a right-click takes what it caught.
task.backcountry.ice_fishing.tip_up: Set a Tip-Up in the ice
task.backcountry.ice_fishing.tip_up.how: Right-click ice over water with the auger to cut a hole, and set the Tip-Up in it.
task.backcountry.ice_fishing.why: Lakes freeze over; the fish under the ice do not.
task.backcountry.land_fish.bait.how: Dig a Worm with a shovel in grass or dirt, most often after rain, and load it into the rod's rig with the hooks.
task.backcountry.land_fish.fish.how: Sneak and right-click the rod to put the line and a hook from your pack on it, then right-click water to cast, and reel in when it bites.
task.backcountry.land_fish.rod.how: 3 Sticks in a diagonal in the crafting grid.
task.backcountry.land_fish.why: A large pike is almost 2,000 kcal.
task.backcountry.lay_woodpile.laid.how: Right-click the ground with firewood; 16 fill a pile, and a full pile takes another on top. It dries 12.5% a day, but not while rain or snow falls on it: roof it.
task.backcountry.lay_woodpile.split.how: A log with its bark and the axe in the crafting grid make 2 pieces.
task.backcountry.lay_woodpile.why: Wood dries on a woodpile, and dry wood burns longer and hotter.
task.backcountry.light_fire.bow_drill.ho: Two Sticks, a Cordage and a Softwood in the crafting grid.
task.backcountry.light_fire.campfire: Build a Campfire and set it down
task.backcountry.light_fire.campfire.how: Three Sticks over three logs in the crafting grid, then place it.
task.backcountry.light_fire.fed.how: Right-click the fire with Softwood; it holds 4 pieces.
task.backcountry.light_fire.lit.how: Carry the Tinder Bundle and 2 Sticks and right-click the campfire with the Bow Drill (A and D saw; Space blows on the ember, gently) or the Ferro Rod.
task.backcountry.light_fire.log.how: Break a spruce log with the axe; the whole tree falls.
task.backcountry.light_fire.softwood.how: A spruce log and the axe in the crafting grid make 2 Softwood. Fresh Softwood catches; fresh Hardwood is too green.
task.backcountry.light_fire.tinder.how: Right-click a birch log with the axe to peel Birch Bark. Two bark and a Plant Fibre make the bundle.
task.backcountry.light_fire.why: A fire warms and dries you, cooks and boils water.
task.backcountry.make_arrows.arrows.how: A Stick, a feather and Flint make a Broadhead Arrow.
task.backcountry.make_arrows.feather.how: Birds drop them: grouse, ptarmigan, geese and ducks.
task.backcountry.make_arrows.why: Broadheads kill; blunt arrows take small game.
task.backcountry.make_bow.bow.how: The seasoned stave, the Bowstring and the knife in the crafting grid.
task.backcountry.make_bow.seasoned.how: Season it on a lit campfire for 5 minutes.
task.backcountry.make_bow.stave.how: A hardwood log and the knife in the crafting grid.
task.backcountry.make_bow.why: An arrow to the chest brings down game of any size.
task.backcountry.make_knife.flint.how: Break gravel by lakes and rivers; flint drops 1 time in 10.
task.backcountry.make_knife.knife: Make the Knife, or carry the Belt Knife
task.backcountry.make_knife.knife.how: Flint, a Stick and a Cordage in the crafting grid.
task.backcountry.make_knife.why: The knife dresses game, scrapes hides and cuts stakes.
task.backcountry.make_pemmican.fat.how: Boil animal fat in the Cooking Pot.
Dried meat or fish, Rendered Fat and berries in the crafting grid make 2.
task.backcountry.make_pemmican.why: Dried meat, fat and berries: the most food for the least weight, and the fat a lean winter lacks.
task.backcountry.reach_april.reached.how: Keep the fire fed and eat from the caches.
task.backcountry.reach_april.why: By April the worst of the cold is behind you.
task.backcountry.reach_may.reached.how: The year's summary shows, and the team's goals start again.
task.backcountry.reach_may.why: A whole year on the island.
task.backcountry.sleep_roofed.roof.how: Any blocks within 4 overhead make a roof; dense spruce counts too.
task.backcountry.sleep_roofed.slept.how: At night under the roof, sneak and right-click the ground, or use the Sleeping Bag or Pad.
task.backcountry.sleep_roofed.why: A roof keeps rain, frost and wind off a night's sleep.
task.backcountry.smelt_iron.ingot.how: Put raw iron in the furnace with charcoal or wood below.
task.backcountry.smelt_iron.raw.how: Dig iron-flecked gravel with a shovel: in the birch forests' gravel pits and the beds of streams and lakes. One dig in 4 turns up Raw Iron.
task.backcountry.smelt_iron.why: Iron makes snare wire, hooks, the Cooking Pot and the ice auger.
task.backcountry.smoke_meat.smoked.how: Hang raw meat or fish in it and feed it wood that catches; after 12 hours of rising smoke it comes out smoked.
task.backcountry.smoke_meat.smoker: Build a Smoker and set it down
task.backcountry.smoke_meat.smoker.how: 2 Cordage, 3 logs, a Campfire and 3 cobblestone in the crafting grid.
task.backcountry.smoke_meat.why: Smoked meat keeps for months: food for the winter.
task.backcountry.spruce_tea.drunk.how: Put the needles in a Camp Pot of water and boil it over a fire.
task.backcountry.spruce_tea.needles.how: Break spruce leaves with the knife.
task.backcountry.spruce_tea.why: Spruce tea keeps scurvy off when no berries grow.
task.backcountry.take_animal.dressed.how: Sneak and right-click it with an empty hand to carry it; set it down and click it with the knife.
task.backcountry.take_animal.killed.how: An arrow to the chest kills; any other hit wounds it, and it bleeds a trail you can follow.
task.backcountry.take_animal.why: A moose feeds you for weeks, a hare for a day.
task.backcountry.tall_cache.cache: Set a Food Cache on the poles
task.backcountry.tall_cache.cache.how: Stack 3 stripped logs and put the cache on top. A ladder beside the poles lets climbers in, so take it down.
task.backcountry.tall_cache.poles.how: Use an axe on a log to strip its bark.
task.backcountry.tall_cache.why: Bears, wolverines and mice can't climb poles: food up high stays yours.
task.backcountry.track_animal.sign.how: Sneak and look at a print or droppings a few hours old or fresher.
task.backcountry.track_animal.stalked.ho: Come within 32 blocks of a moose or caribou before it catches your scent.
task.backcountry.track_animal.why: Fresh sign leads to game; stalk it into the wind.
task.backcountry.track_animal.wind.how: Sneak + right-click with Plant Fibre: the strands drift downwind.
task.backcountry.trap_catch: Take a catch from a snare
task.backcountry.trap_catch.catch.how: Check it the next day; a right-click takes what it caught.
task.backcountry.trap_catch.set.how: Snare Wire and Trap Stakes; set it on the ground where hares run. On fresh hare prints in snow it catches twice as often; a Cricket baits it.
task.backcountry.trap_catch.stakes.how: 2 Sticks and the knife in the crafting grid.
task.backcountry.trap_catch.why: Snares catch while you do other work.
task.backcountry.trap_catch.wire.how: An Iron Ingot alone in the crafting grid makes 9 Iron Nuggets; 2 nuggets twist into a Snare Wire.
tooltip.backcountry.binoculars: Hold use or %s to look through them
tooltip.backcountry.dried: Dried: eaten as it is, light to carry, keeps for months
tooltip.backcountry.headlamp_charge: %s of light · lights in the dark
tooltip.backcountry.headlamp_wind: Hold use to wind it, wear it to light the way
tooltip.backcountry.hint.akutaq: Fat, berries and snow whipped together: keeps frozen
tooltip.backcountry.hint.bark_map: Use to read · sneak and hold use to survey: daylight, no rain or snow, and a piece of charcoal
tooltip.backcountry.hint.bone_marrow: Crack a bone with a rock: rich in fat
tooltip.backcountry.hint.bow_saw: Fells and splits in half the time
tooltip.backcountry.hint.canoe: Two seats, faster than a raft · a gale can tip you out
tooltip.backcountry.hint.clams: Dug from beach sand with a shovel · shellfish can poison, most of all in summer, and cooking doesn't help
tooltip.backcountry.hint.drying_rack: Hang raw meat or fish: it dries in 2 dry days, twice as fast over a fire
tooltip.backcountry.hint.ferro_rod: Lights tinder and kindling at once
tooltip.backcountry.hint.fish_wheel: Set in a stream two blocks deep · up to 4 salmon a day in the run, a whitefish or grayling otherwise
tooltip.backcountry.hint.fur_mittens: Worn in the hands slot: keeps hands from going numb
tooltip.backcountry.hint.fur_parka: Warmest coat · the hood keeps your head warm under a headlamp
tooltip.backcountry.hint.game_guts: Bait for hooks and the Tip-Up · raw, they make you sick 1 time in 4
tooltip.backcountry.hint.goose_egg: From goose nests by the lakes in May
tooltip.backcountry.hint.hide_mittens: Worn in the hands slot: keeps hands from going numb
tooltip.backcountry.hint.mussels: Picked from stony shores · shellfish can poison, most of all in summer, and cooking doesn't help
tooltip.backcountry.hint.pitch_salve: Heals an infected wound or burns within a day
tooltip.backcountry.hint.pitch_tinder: Catches in rain: the bow drill works wet
tooltip.backcountry.hint.salt: Craft with raw meat or fish to salt it: it keeps 8 times as long
tooltip.backcountry.hint.sharpening_ston: Craft with a worn knife, axe or saw to sharpen it
tooltip.backcountry.hint.sleeping_bags.b: Sleep warm anywhere at night · use it on the ground to lie down
tooltip.backcountry.hint.sleeping_pad: Keeps the cold ground off while you sleep · use it on the ground at night to lie down
tooltip.backcountry.hint.smouldering_fun: Smoulders for two hours · lights a cold fire with tinder and kindling, no bow drill
tooltip.backcountry.hint.spruce_pitch: Weeps from a spruce blaze after two days: scrape it off with a knife
tooltip.backcountry.hint.spruce_roots: Dug with a shovel beside a spruce: lashing for a canoe
tooltip.backcountry.hint.stone_chimney: Stack above a Stone Fireplace or campfire up through the roof: the smoke leaves, the room stays sealed
tooltip.backcountry.hint.stone_fireplace: Burns firewood like a campfire on half the wood; needs a chimney or open sky above
tooltip.backcountry.hint.tarp: A thin roof: keeps the rain and wind off
tooltip.backcountry.hint.wolverine_pelt: Frost brushes off wolverine fur: the ruff for a Fur Parka
tooltip.backcountry.raw: Raw: parasites 3 times in 5. Cook it on a fire.
tooltip.backcountry.render_fat: Roast it on a fire, or render 2 in the Cooking Pot to keep it for months.
tooltip.backcountry.sea_water: Sea water · %s: boil it dry on a fire for salt
tooltip.backcountry.seasoned: %s%% seasoned · catches from %s%%, burns hotter the drier
tooltip.backcountry.too_green: Too green to catch: dry it on a woodpile
woodpile.backcountry.drying: Dries %s%% a day while no rain or snow falls on it
